searchedFor: Grep 'dryRun' in packages/cli/src (no hits in commands/api-keys.ts)
finding.summary: `api-keys revoke`/`create` still ignore `--dry-run` and execute the mutation
finding.evidence: This change adds `opts.dryRun` short-circuits to read commands, but `registerApiKeysCommand` has no `dryRun` check at all: `api-keys create <name>` (api-keys.ts:17 → `createApiKey`) and `api-keys revoke <key-id>` (api-keys.ts:45 → `revokeApiKey`, a DELETE) run the real request under `--dry-run`. A user (or agent) previewing `wafflebase api-keys revoke k-1 --dry-run` irreversibly revokes the key, even though the global flag is documented as 'Show request without executing' (root.ts:75) and docs/design/cli.md advertises dry-run as a first-class agent affordance. A grep for `dryRun` across packages/cli/src returns zero hits in api-keys.ts.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts has no dry-run handling at all — it never imports printDryRun and never reads opts.dryRun. `create` calls createApiKey unconditionally (api-keys.ts:17) and `revoke` calls revokeApiKey (a DELETE) unconditionally (api-keys.ts:45), even though getGlobalOpts is called at api-keys.ts:15/29/43 and GlobalOpts carries dryRun (root.ts:21) from the global flag documented as 'Show request without executing' (root.ts:75). I searched for an indirect guard and found none: cli.ts registers the command plainly and calls parseAsync with no commander preAction hook (cli.ts:29, cli.ts:76; the only 'hook' match in src is a prose comment at root.ts:49); getConfig never forwards dryRun into CliConfig (root.ts:29-36); and HttpClient.createApiKey/revokeApiKey fetch immediately with no dry-run branch (http-client.ts:372-389). printDryRun is a pure printer only invoked from command actions (client/dry-run.ts:6-25), and every other namespace does call it (docs.ts:5, slides.ts:5, notes.ts:5, files.ts:4, cells.ts:4, tabs.ts:4, sheets-import.ts:6) — api-keys is the sole omission. The CLI's own schema marks api-keys.revoke safety: 'destructive' (registry.ts:591-593), so previewing with --dry-run irreversibly revokes the key: unrecoverable data loss on a real path, critical under the correctness lens.

searchedFor: Grep 'dryRun' across packages/cli/src to enumerate commands with/without the guard
Read packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts, slides.ts (lines 20-150), files.ts in full
finding.summary: The same `--dry-run`-still-fetches bug is left unfixed in notes/slides/files read commands
finding.evidence: The change fixes `docs list`, `docs get`, `tabs list` and `cells get`, but identical read commands elsewhere still hit the network under `--dry-run`: `notes get` (notes.ts:76 `getDocument`), `notes list` (notes.ts:35 `listDocuments`), `slides get` (slides.ts:81), `slides list` (slides.ts:40), `files list` (files.ts:85) and `files get` (files.ts:105). Each of these has no `opts.dryRun` branch, so `--dry-run` performs the very request it promises not to send — the same behavior this PR describes as a bug (burnt rate limit, access-log entry). The fix is partial and leaves the flag's semantics inconsistent across sibling namespaces.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: there is no global dry-run interception anywhere in the CLI — getClient() (commands/root.ts:38-40) builds a plain HttpClient, HttpClient.request() (client/http-client.ts:166-186) always fetches, printDryRun (client/dry-run.ts:6-25) is a pure printer, and cli.ts:17-92 installs no preAction hook. The six cited read actions therefore reach the network under --dry-run: notes.ts:35 (list) and notes.ts:76 (get), slides.ts:40 (list) and slides.ts:81 (get), files.ts:85 (list) and files.ts:105 (get) all call the client with no `if (opts.dryRun)` branch, unlike their siblings in the same files (notes.ts:55/89/107/135/195, slides.ts:60/94/112/141/197, files.ts:58/118/136). The contract broken is stated globally, not per-command: docs/design/cli.md:809-810 ("prints the request that would be sent — without executing it") and cli.md:824-827 ("A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless"). The task doc's non-goals (20260816-cli-dry-run-read-commands-todo.md:32-36) only exempt commands that *already* honour the flag, which these do not. Against an unreachable server these commands emit `fetch failed` / non-zero exit instead of the documented dry_run envelope — wrong runtime behavior for a documented flag, in the correctness lane. No counterexample found after searching the whole packages/cli/src tree for dryRun, hooks, and client-level guards.
